title: Finite reduction of purity
statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
$1\leq m\leq n$, and write $\operatorname{red}_{n,m,T}$ for the finite
reduction functor

$$
K\mapsto K\otimes^L_{A_{E,n}}A_{E,m}:\
D^b_{ctf}(T,A_{E,n})\longrightarrow D^b_{ctf}(T,A_{E,m})
$$

on a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $T$. For a smooth separated
morphism $f:X\to Y$ between separated finite-type $k$-schemes, of pure
relative dimension $d$ and $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A_{E,n})$, the square

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}\operatorname{red}_{n,m,X}\bigl(Lf^*K(d)[2d]\bigr)
& \xrightarrow{\ \operatorname{red}_{n,m}(\gamma_{f,K})\ }& \operatorname{red}_{n,m,X}(Rf^!K)\\
\big\downarrow\ \sim
& & \big\downarrow\ \sim\\
Lf^*\operatorname{red}_{n,m,Y}K(d)[2d]
& \xrightarrow{\ \gamma_{f,\operatorname{red}_{n,m}K}\ }& Rf^!_{A_{E,m}}\operatorname{red}_{n,m,Y}K
\end{array}$$

commutes, the vertical isomorphisms being the finite-reduction
compatibilities of the six-operations package. The same is true for the
affine orientations of [thm-pur-affine-line-orientation], the smooth
traces of [def-pur-smooth-trace], the composition coherence of
[thm-pur-composition-coherence], and the base-change squares of
[thm-pur-smooth-base-change-coherence].

proof.text: Use the intrinsic reassociation square [lem-pur-finite-reduction-reassociation-intrinsic] and the tensor-form purity square [lem-pur-finite-reduction-tensor-purity]. Both use the explicitly constructed same intermediate tensor-source comparison [def-pur-finite-reduction-tensor-source]. Unfold smoothPurityMap as realized tau followed by smoothPurityTensorMap [def-pur-smooth-purity-map]. Functor.map_comp and associativity paste the two squares to give finiteReductionOfPurity, with exactly the original source and exceptional comparisons.

Apply [lem-pur-finite-diagonal-orientation-reduction] to the zero section and to $W=X\times_YX$ with its diagonal. It identifies the reduced supported affine orientation and its products, and identifies each arrow of the normalized diagonal chain, so $Q\alpha_f=\alpha_{f,B}$. Thus the affine-orientation clause already holds.

source.place: Steps 3-4: supported Kummer and diagonal normalization

proof.text: The trace is the compact-support image of gamma followed by the exceptional counit [def-pur-smooth-trace]. Naturality of the actual scalar-adjunction compact-support comparison follows by transposing its defining restriction-comparison naturality square. The chosen exceptional comparison satisfies its counit equation [def-pur-finite-reduction-comparisons]. Rewrite the reduced counit by that equation, move reduced gamma across the compact-support comparison by naturality, apply the main purity reduction square, and combine functorial images. This proves finiteReductionOfSmoothTrace. For the coefficient-unit trace, transport the ordinary-etale constructible finite-Tor unit through the preservation clause of [lem-coef-finite-hom-site-descent]. The canonical exact-derived composite isomorphism identifies its image with coefficientUnit; [lem-weil-proetale-dbc-triangulated] supplies isomorphism closure of intrinsic constructibility, and the definition of Tor amplitude transports its representative isomorphisms. The universal presentation equation of smoothPurityTensorMap identifies smoothTrace with coefficientValuedSmoothTrace at that unit. Naturality of the transported exceptional counit follows from its published pro-etale naturality, compact-support comparison naturality and the intrinsic equivalence counit. Combine it with the proved input naturality of purity [prop-pur-smooth-purity-naturality-cover] to obtain coefficient-valued trace naturality. Apply finiteReductionOfSmoothTrace at the unit, postcompose with the actual finiteReductionUnitComparison, apply trace naturality at the smaller level, and regroup the compact-support functor images. This proves finiteReductionOfUnitSmoothTrace with the original source and unit comparisons.

For finiteReductionOfCompositionCoherence, apply the main purity reduction square to f ≫ g in dimension d+e. Rewrite gamma_(f≫g) by [thm-pur-composition-coherence] at both coefficient levels. This gives exactly the full three-arrow composition path with the originally specified source and exceptional composition isomorphisms, without separate coefficient-reduction identities for those two outer isomorphisms. The two previously stated separate comparison identities have no Lean consumers and no DAG parent needs their stronger conclusions, so prune these surplus auxiliary declarations; retain all six blueprint-clause declarations. For base change, [def-pur-smooth-pullback-exchange] defines the exchange as inverse pulled-back purity, the canonical source arrow, then purity at f prime. Apply [lem-pur-finite-reduction-base-change-source] to the middle source arrow. The actual pullback coefficient comparison is a component of a natural isomorphism, so its naturality and the main purity square give the left purity square. The main purity square at f prime and input naturality of purity [prop-pur-smooth-purity-naturality-cover] give the right purity square, including the coefficient pullback input comparison. Cancel the reduced first purity isomorphism and paste these three squares. This proves both conjuncts of finiteReductionOfBaseChange from the independent source-square lemma. No condition on v is used.

on a $k$-scheme $T$. For a smooth separated $f:X\to Y$ of relative

commutes, the vertical isomorphisms being the finite-reduction

proof.text:
Step 1: the purity map is determined fibrewise, so the comparison may be
made on the geometric fibres. The value of the smooth purity map
[def-pur-smooth-purity-map] over a geometric point $\bar y\to Y$
is prescribed by the purity of the geometric fibre $X_{\bar y}$, which
is the affine-space case [cor-pur-affine-space-zero-section-purity]
together with the rank-one computation
[thm-pur-affine-line-orientation]. Two natural transformations
between the same pair of exact functors of $K$ that agree on every
geometric fibre agree: the strict henselizations of $Y$ at its
geometric points are pro-etale over $Y$ and jointly surjective, hence
form a pro-etale covering family, and isomorphy of a morphism of
complexes of pro-etale sheaves is local for covering families, clause
(1) of [lem-cbc-proetale-stalk-conservative]; it is
therefore enough to compare the two composites of the square fibrewise,
which the compatibilities below do.
Step 2: the reduction compatibilities of the operations. All these
constructions are built from the operations of the six-operations
package, whose finite-reduction compatibilities

$$
(Lf^*K)_m\cong Lf_m^*K_m,\qquad
(Rf^!K)_m\cong Rf_m^!K_m,\qquad
(K(d))_m\cong K_m(d)
$$

are natural in $K$ and in the morphism, by
[def-weil-derived-tensor] and
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] (finite reduction is the derived tensor product along
$A_{E,n}\to A_{E,m}$; this ring map need not be flat, and the
finite-Tor condition is essential for boundedness). The reduction
functor does land in $D^b_{ctf}(T,A_{E,m})$ with the same Tor interval:
if $K$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ it has a bounded flat model in
degrees $[a,b]$ by [lem-sf-flat-model], and the reduction of that model
is a bounded flat model of $K_m$ in $[a,b]$ by
[lem-sf-reduction-flat-model]. Compatibility
with pullback and the invertible twist follows from associativity
of derived tensor. For the smooth exceptional inverse image use
the previously constructed tensor formula and its coefficient
compatibility, rather than flat base change. The composition
identifications are those of
[def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] (the functoriality of
$R^!$ and of the composition isomorphisms), and by
[def-coefficient-twists-detailed] (the coefficient twists are reduced
coefficient twists). Step 3: the glueing data reduce. The sheaf
axiom gluing used in [thm-pur-dnc-invariance] is a statement
about finite locally constant rank-one sheaves, and the reduction of a
finite locally constant rank-one sheaf is again one; the local
normalizations of [thm-pur-dnc-invariance] are the reductions of
the normalizations, the lisse-uniqueness of
[lem-pur-lisse-uniqueness] reduces, and the splitting-principle
descent of one element of an abelian group used in
[thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object] reduces for the same reason
(the Künneth and supported-cohomology groups of
[lem-pur-kunneth-supported] are compatible with the coefficient
reduction, the boundary of the Kummer class reducing to the boundary
of the reduced Kummer class). Hence the vertical isomorphisms of the
square identify $\operatorname{red}_{n,m}(\gamma_{f,K})$ with
$\gamma_{f,\operatorname{red}_{n,m}K}$, which is the commutativity
of the displayed square. Step 4: the remaining statements. The
affine orientations of [thm-pur-affine-line-orientation] are
constructed from the Kummer boundary, whose reduction is the boundary
of the reduced Kummer class, i.e. the reduction of the orientation;
the smooth trace of [def-pur-smooth-trace] reduces because the
counit of the adjunction reduces (the adjunction itself is compatible
with the finite reduction of the coefficient ring); the composition
and base-change coherence statements are the compatible systems
obtained from Steps 1–3 applied to the constituents of the two
squares.
